The Desert has none, though The Hope Entity describes its light, weather, distance, and scale as state-driven.
Environments generally. Every reference currently in the vault is a character or a sigil. No location art exists.


Open Questions

What is the silhouette rule that makes Subject-001 and Subject-002 readable as related but distinct at a glance?
How is a straitjacket animated for a playable or semi-playable figure without it reading as comedy?
What does temporal desynchronization look like in an environment — visible seams, doubled geometry, mismatched lighting, or something quieter?
Is the shadow form a full model swap, a material change, or a lighting effect?
What is the render target — stylized realism, painterly, high-contrast?
Where do the images actually live? _Img currently uses default Pasted image <timestamp> names, which will not scale past a few dozen assets.

Animation Mechanics
Tags: project-zaman production production design animation dodge parry proposed


                  
                  Purpose 
                  
                

This note defines a combat-animation direction for Project ZAMAN: contextual defensive animations that react to the opponent’s attack instead of using one generic dodge or parry response.



Design Goal
Project ZAMAN’s combat should feel grounded, readable, and tense.
Defensive animation can support that by making the player character respond to the specific threat in front of him. A horizontal sweep, a direct thrust, an overhead strike, and a low attack should not all trigger the same body motion.
The goal is realism through response quality, not animation excess.

Variant Dodge Mechanics
Variant Dodge Mechanics activate dedicated dodge animations based on the opponent’s incoming attack.
The system can read several attack properties:

Attack height: high, mid, or low.
Attack line: horizontal, vertical, thrusting, circular, or diagonal.
Attack source: weapon, limb, projectile, grab, or environmental hazard.
Player direction: forward, backward, left, right, or angled.
Timing quality: early, clean, late, or panic input.
Distance: close pressure, normal range, or barely-in-range evasion.

This allows defensive movement to look intentional:

































Incoming attackPossible dodge responseHorizontal sweepDuck, shoulder roll, or compact side slipStraight thrustNarrow sidestep or angled pivotOverhead strikeBack step, shoulder turn, or diagonal escapeLow sweepHop, lifted step, or backward pullGrab attemptHand break, torso twist, or short shove-awayProjectileLean, drop, side roll, or cover-aware evade
The animation should never hide the player’s intention. Even when a contextual variant plays, the input direction and timing still need to be clear.

Variant Parry Mechanics
Variant Parry Mechanics use dedicated parry reactions based on the incoming attack’s angle, force, and source.
A strong parry system should not make every successful defense look like the same weapon tap. It should show how Subject-001 survives pressure while still appearing physically vulnerable.
Possible variants:

































Incoming attackPossible parry responseLight weapon strikeQuick deflection with minimal recoveryHeavy weapon strikeTwo-handed brace, recoil, or staggered redirectThrustOutside-line deflection or wrist turnOverhead strikeRaised guard, angled catch, or shoulder dropClaw or limb attackForearm jam, body slip, or elbow checkRepeated combo hitChain parry with rising stamina or posture cost
The parry should reward accurate timing while still respecting the fiction. A perfect response can look skillful, but not effortless.

Readability Rules

Do not let contextual animations steal control for too long.
Keep dodge and parry outcomes readable at boss speed.
Use clear anticipation frames on enemy attacks so the player can learn patterns.
Match animation intensity to risk: a late dodge should look less composed than a clean one.
Preserve the Soulslike demand for commitment, stamina, spacing, and recovery.
Avoid making defensive variety purely cosmetic; the chosen variant should communicate why it worked.


Lore Fit
This system suits Subject-001 because his survival is not based on brute confidence.
He carries inherited grief, fragmented identity, and a body moving through danger without full certainty. Contextual dodge and parry animations can express that: not invincible grace, but precise survival under pressure.
The system should also respect the broader premise of Immaculate Thought and the calm requirement recorded in Mechanics Index. If defensive mastery ever connects to calm, it should feel like controlled presence rather than aggression.

Game Design Index
Tags: project-zaman production production design open


                  
                  Purpose of this folder 
                  
                

How Project ZAMAN plays. Everything here is implementation-facing; the fiction it draws on lives in Lore/ and World/.



Established

































Genre3D Action / Adventure · SoulslikeEngineUndecided · New Input SystemAesthetic referencesLies of P, BloodbornePlayer characterSubject-001 — the soul-dominant fragmentCiviliansNone. Settlement regions are protected territories, faction outposts, or remnants of organized activityAnimation directionAnimation Mechanics - contextual dodge and parry variants based on incoming attacks
Source: Project Zaman, Subject-001, The Oasis.

The One System That Is Actually Designed
The Oasis contains a complete faction system — seven player paths with consequences, NPC behavior split by solo versus grouped, a two-stage looting system where the second attempt provokes fury because the remaining item is personal, and a “best” outcome that requires the player to prove both factions hold incomplete halves of the same answer.
It is the most production-ready document in the vault. Everything below is comparatively undefined.

Systems Not Yet Designed
Combat. The full system is still open. Animation Mechanics now establishes one concrete direction: variant dodge and parry animations that respond to the opponent’s attack. Stamina, posture or poise, weapon movesets, and the checkpoint-and-recovery loop still need design.
The miracles as mechanics. MC establishes that all three require internal calm and degrade under fear, grief, anger, and panic. Open Gaps #02 settles that Subject-001 does not directly inherit them, while their broader post-fission fate remains unresolved. If any miracle becomes playable, the design must explain how it returns, echoes, or operates through a changed form.
The shadow form. Open Gaps #07 asks whether it can be resisted, accelerated, or redirected through player choice. A risk-reward transformation is the obvious reading, but nothing is decided.
The Desert and the Hope Entity. The Hope Entity specifies conditions that bring the entity nearer or push it further, tied to Subject-001’s coherence rather than his mood. That is a legible progression system in all but name. Open Gaps #04 asks whether reconnection is one event or a gradual process, and whether the player can fail or delay it.
Subject-002 encounters. Established as only ever seen at a distance. Whether that is a scripted sighting, a wandering presence, or something the player can pursue is unresolved — as is their eventual relationship, Open Gaps #03.
Death and recovery. The Irreversibility Principle says nothing is restored. A genre built on repeated death and retrieval sits in direct tension with that. Worth resolving deliberately rather than by default.

Open Questions

What is the core combat loop, and what does the player actually hold?
Do the miracles become abilities, or stay narrative?
What is the cost of using one? Nothing in the vault describes fatigue or backlash.
How does the game express calm as a mechanical state the player manages?
What does dying mean in a world where nothing is restored?
Is the Desert a playable space, a cutscene, or a recurring interstitial?
Scope: how many locations, bosses, and hours is this actually aiming at?


Suggested Notes for This Folder

Core Loop
Combat System
Animation Mechanics
The Calm State — the miracle precondition, as a managed resource
Miracles as Abilities
Shadow Form Mechanics
Desert and Hope Entity Progression
Faction System — extract from The Oasis once it stabilizes
NPC Encounter Design
Death, Recovery, and the Irreversibility Principle
Scope and Vertical Slice




                  
                  The design question worth answering first 
                  
                

This game’s abilities are switched off by fear, anger, and panic. Its genre is built on producing exactly those states in the player. Deciding whether that is a contradiction to solve or the entire point will determine most of the systems above.

Color Language
Tags: project-zaman symbols symbol color working


                  
                  Purpose of this folder 
                  
                

The meaning color carries in Project ZAMAN, and the rules that keep it consistent across art, UI, and environment. A color only means something if it is withheld elsewhere.



Colors Already Used in the Vault
Every entry below is drawn from an existing note. Nothing here is a decided system yet — it is the raw material a system could be built from.













































ColorWhere it already appearsSourceWhiteThe Gibborim serpent: purity, revelation, divine authority — concealing the violence beneathGibborimBlackThe Axios serpent: silent observation, precision, knowledge without declared intentAxiosBlack and white togetherAlyna’s vintage maid uniform — her passport and her invisibility cloak. People see the uniform before they see herAlyna, Story StructureRedThe shadow form: eyes completely red with intensified blood flowStory StructureGlow / lightThe Hope Entity, seen as a glowing figure at the end of the DesertStory Structure, The Hope EntitySandThe Desert itself — every grain a moment loosened from its sequenceStory StructureShimmerShimmering skin with sigil markings, on the post-fission entityProject Zaman

The Pattern Worth Noticing
The two cult colors are already an opposed pair with assigned meanings, and Alyna wears both at once. Whether that is deliberate is currently unanswered, but it is the most interesting color fact in the vault: the one genuinely good person in the story wears the cult’s two colors as a uniform, and it is precisely that uniform that lets her move unseen through their building.
Worth deciding whether this is coincidence or the spine of the whole color system.

Working Faction Palettes
These are practical starting points, not final canon.




















FactionCore colorsMeaningThe Order of the OasisDeep green, worn brass, off-white cloth, dark leatherProtected life, discipline, inherited duty, and controlled survival.The MirageSun-faded blue, ash gray, weathered black, pale clothDistance, dust, uncertainty, fieldwork, and truth seen through distortion.
The two child factions should share traces of the parent Oasis palette, but each should damage or preserve it differently. The Order keeps the mark controlled and upright. The Mirage lets it waver, break, or fade.

Open Questions

Is there a color for the protagonist? He is excluded from the cult’s naming system. Excluding him from its palette as well would be consistent — but then what is he? Absence of color, or a color the cult has no use for?
What separates Subject-001 from Subject-002 visually? They share an origin and need to read as different at a glance, especially since Subject-002 is only ever seen at a distance.
How final are the two successor palettes? The Order and The Mirage now have working palettes, but they still need testing against character designs, environments, and UI readability.
Does the Desert have a palette that changes? The Hope Entity establishes that its light, weather, and scale shift with Subject-001’s coherence. That is a color system waiting to be written.
What does a colliding era look like in color? The one chance to make temporal desynchronization readable without dialogue.
Is red reserved? If red belongs only to the shadow form, it cannot be used for UI, blood, or enemies without weakening it.


Suggested Structure
Rather than one note per color, this folder may work better as:

Core Palette — the small set of colors with fixed meaning, and what each is forbidden to be used for
Faction Palettes — Anthropos, Gibborim, Axios, the Order, The Mirage
Character Palettes — including whether the MC has one
The Desert Palette — state-driven rather than fixed
UI and Readability — where meaning has to give way to legibility




                  
                  Rule to hold the system together 
                  
                

Assign each color one meaning and then protect it by not using it elsewhere. A palette in a story like this fails through overuse, not through poor choices.

Established Sigils
The White Serpent — Gibborim

Anthropos — No Public Symbol
Anthropos displays nothing. Worth treating as a deliberate design statement rather than an omission: the layer that touches the public is the layer that leaves no mark. A charity does not need a sigil; it needs a letterhead.

Other Marks Already in the Vault

The letter crate markings — the cult’s markings on the ornate crate that paid for a sold child. Alyna recognizes them instantly. The only time a sigil functions as evidence in the story.

project-zaman/symbols/typography/typogra.content:
Typography and Written Language
Tags: project-zaman symbols symbol language naming working


                  
                  Purpose of this folder 
                  
                

Two related things: the in-world writing systems (which language belongs to whom, and what that ownership means), and the typographic direction for the game itself — titles, item text, UI, subtitles.
The first is already half-designed. The second is untouched.



The Naming Framework — Established
From Project Zaman, Core Principle 01:






























LanguageReserved forStatusArabicCore metaphysical truths, world concepts, protagonist-facing ideasDeclared, no terms written yetHebrewThe cult, its rituals, ranks, doctrines, chambers, subjects, esoteric terminologyIn use — Gibborim, NoamGreekThe public-facing layerIn use — Anthropos, AxiosNoneThe protagonistDeliberate. The [[MC
Gibborim extends this: Axios’ clinical designations (Subject-001, Subject-002) begin as neutral archival identifiers and are then absorbed into Gibborim’s ceremonial framework. Within the inner order a number is never merely a number — it carries sequence, proximity, failure, inheritance, and perceived worth.
So the vault already has three registers of written language, each with a different relationship to truth:

Greek speaks to the public and is meant to be read
Hebrew speaks inward and is meant to exclude
Axios’ clinical script claims to be neutral and is the most dishonest of the three


The Gap
Arabic is assigned the most important category — core metaphysical truths and everything the protagonist faces — and currently contains zero terms. Every named thing in the vault is Hebrew, Greek, or plain English.
This is the single largest hole in the naming system, and it matters more than it looks: the framework’s whole point is that the protagonist stands outside the cult’s language. That only lands if there is a language he stands in.
Concepts that would sit in the Arabic register if it existed: Immaculate Thought, Soul Fission, the Oscillation of Eras, the Desert, the Hope Entity, and the Irreversibility Principle.

Open Questions
In-world

Does Zaman itself belong to the Arabic register, and can characters say it?
Should established concepts be renamed into Arabic, given Arabic names alongside their English ones, or left as they are with Arabic reserved for new material?
Who in-world speaks the Arabic register? If nobody does, is it the narration’s language rather than any character’s?
Do the Order of the Oasis and The Mirage have their own written voice? The Order claims the founder’s legacy, so its documents would be formal and preservationist; Mirage field records would be hurried and damaged.

Typographic

What does the title treatment look like — and does it use one script or two?
Item and note text: this is a Soulslike, so item descriptions carry most of the lore. Do they read as Axios’ clinical reports, as recovered Mirage field notes, or as an unattributed narrator?
Does any in-game text appear in a script the player cannot read? A powerful option, given that the story is about being defined in a language you were never given.
Legibility floor for subtitles and UI at the target resolutions.


Suggested Notes for This Folder

The Naming Framework — expanded from Core Principle 01, with a running glossary per language
The Arabic Register — the empty one; probably the highest-value note in this folder
Hebrew Glossary — terms in use and their meanings
Greek Glossary
Axios' Clinical Register — report formatting, designation syntax, how a subject is written about
Game Typography — typefaces, hierarchy, item text voice, UI legibility




                  
                  Constraint already established 
                  
                

Language in this project is a form of ownership. Gibborim names in order to possess; Axios numbers in order to neutralize; the protagonist is left unnamed in order to be excluded. Any new naming decision should answer the question who does this give power to.

project-zaman/world/locations/ashbourne-.title: Ashbourne Children's Home
project-zaman/world/locations/ashbourne-.content:
Ashbourne Children’s Home
Tags: project-zaman world location ashbourne anthropos established
“A charity with a locked second purpose.”
Type: Orphanage; Anthropos acquisition and observation site
Era: Before the Oscillation of Eras
Controlled by: Anthropos
Public Status: Charitable children’s home
True Status: Burned, evacuated, and later revisited by the rescued children
Post-Oscillation Status: Unresolved

Overview
Ashbourne Children’s Home presents itself as an ordinary charitable orphanage: a respectable institution where abandoned children are given shelter, education, and the possibility of adoption.
In truth, Ashbourne forms part of Anthropos’s hidden recruitment and observation network.
The cult uses the orphanage to identify children who display unusual cognitive, spiritual, or soul-based potential. Those considered valuable are documented, monitored, and eventually transferred into more controlled environments through adoption, sponsorship, medical referral, or other publicly acceptable means.
The original MC spends most of his childhood at Ashbourne. His life there changes when Noam reports the first two miracles, leading to the MC’s public adoption, private extraction, and eventual captivity.

Hidden Purpose
Ashbourne serves three purposes within the Anthropos system.
Acquisition
The orphanage gives Anthropos access to children who possess no stable family protection and whose disappearances can be concealed through forged adoption records, transfers, illness reports, or institutional relocation.
Observation
Children are monitored over long periods for unusual patterns in behavior, cognition, intuition, memory, emotional influence, and spiritual sensitivity.
Most are never told they are being studied.
Consequence Analysis
Ashbourne also functions as an early-warning environment.
Anthropos does not fully understand the forces it is attempting to control. Because of this, the cult uses the orphanage to observe what consequences may emerge around unusual children before exposing its primary laboratories, personnel, and research sites.
Minor incidents, behavioral changes, shared dreams, unexplained coincidences, miracles, and disturbances are documented as possible indicators of a larger metaphysical reaction.
Ashbourne therefore becomes both a testing ground and a buffer. If something goes wrong, the event can be blamed on poor management, childhood imagination, illness, fire, institutional neglect, or religious superstition.
The children bear the consequence. The true facilities remain hidden.

The Decoy Institution
Ashbourne is publicly visible by design.
Its existence draws attention away from Anthropos’s more important locations and provides the cult with a believable source for records concerning displaced children. Investigators searching for missing subjects are led toward the orphanage, its fabricated administrators, and its falsified adoption history rather than the facilities where the children are actually taken.
This makes Ashbourne a decoy source in two ways:


It provides a false administrative origin for children already moved into Anthropos custody.


It absorbs suspicion when an experiment, disappearance, or unexplained event threatens to become public.


The orphanage is expendable. Its records, staff identities, and legal ownership can all be abandoned once they become dangerous.

Narrative Function
Ashbourne is the story’s first institutional mask.
It appears to represent care, safety, and public charity. Beneath that surface, it is a sorting mechanism built around children the cult considers useful.
It establishes one of the central truths of Project ZAMAN:

Anthropos rarely hides evil behind darkness.
It hides it behind respectable systems.

Ashbourne is important because:


It is the original MC’s childhood home.


It is the first place where Noam’s assignment becomes morally dangerous.


It introduces Anthropos’s habit of disguising control as protection.


It allows the cult to study possible consequences without exposing its primary facilities.


It becomes the site where Alyna’s resistance and the MC’s third miracle quietly operate in parallel.


Its destruction turns an expendable decoy into a source of evidence the cult can no longer fully contain.



Key Events

















































EventConsequenceNoam is deployed to AshbourneAnthropos places an observer among the children it wishes to study.The first two miracles occurNoam reports the incidents, causing the MC to be marked for extraction.The third miracle remains unnoticedAnthropos removes the MC before understanding the full nature of his abilities.The public adoptionThe MC is taken into Noam’s family under the appearance of charity and social advancement.The targeted fire beginsAnthropos attempts to destroy a specific compartment and erase dangerous evidence.The fire spreadsA controlled destruction becomes a public disaster, increasing scrutiny around the orphanage.Alyna rescues the childrenThe intended casualties survive, preventing Anthropos from closing the incident cleanly.Ashbourne remains abandonedFor three days, the damaged building is left empty and unrepaired.The children returnThey recover personal belongings and unknowingly scatter documents and physical evidence beyond the cult’s control.The post-escape reunionThe MC reconnects with the Ashbourne boys, who recognize the familiar sensation of his silent communication.

The Ashbourne Fire
The fire does not begin as an attempt to destroy the entire orphanage.
It starts inside a targeted compartment containing something Anthropos considers too dangerous to preserve. The intended destruction is controlled, limited, and designed to appear accidental.
The fire spreads beyond its original boundary.
Once the incident becomes visible to the public, Anthropos is forced to distance itself from the institution. Staff records collapse into invented identities, ownership trails lead nowhere, and the orphanage is temporarily abandoned.
For three days, the building remains burned, unsecured, and unrepaired.
During this period, the rescued children return to retrieve their belongings. Without understanding their importance, they carry away damaged papers, labelled objects, fragments of records, and other materials from the building.
What Anthropos intended to erase is instead dispersed.

What Is Known


Ashbourne operates as a legitimate public orphanage.


Its true ownership is concealed behind shell organisations, false records, and invented names.


The institution is connected to Anthropos’s recruitment network.


Children are observed for unusual cognitive, spiritual, and soul-based traits.


Noam is placed inside Ashbourne as an observer.


The original MC is selected after the first two miracles are reported.


Anthropos fails to understand the third miracle before extracting him.


The orphanage acts as a decoy administrative source for children transferred into cult custody.


It is also used to study possible consequences before similar risks are introduced into primary facilities.


The fire begins inside a targeted compartment but spreads into a larger public disaster.


The building remains empty for three days following the fire.


The children later return and unknowingly scatter evidence beyond the cult’s immediate reach.



Thematic Meaning
Ashbourne represents protection without safety.
The children are fed, housed, and educated, yet every act of care is compromised by the institution’s hidden purpose. They are not protected because their lives are valued. They are preserved because they may become useful.
The orphanage also reflects Anthropos’s fear of consequences.
The cult presents itself as confident and enlightened, but Ashbourne reveals its uncertainty. Anthropos is willing to experiment with forces it does not understand, provided someone else stands close enough to suffer first.

Open Questions


Does Ashbourne still exist after the Oscillation of Eras?


Can the player visit its remains during the playable present?


Was the targeted compartment an archive, dormitory, hidden laboratory, observation room, or something else?


What evidence did the children remove from the building?


Did any surviving records eventually reach journalists, authorities, or rival organisations?


Was the spreading fire genuinely accidental, or was it influenced by the MC’s third miracle?


Did Anthropos ever restore Ashbourne’s public reputation?


Was Ashbourne the only institution of its kind?


Did the cult abandon the orphanage after the fire, or continue using it under another name?


What specific consequence was Anthropos afraid might occur there?

Desert
Tags: project-zaman world location desert identity hope established
”Every grain is a moment loosened from its place.”
Type: Psychological landscape
Era: Before and after the Oscillation, inwardly
Belongs to: Subject-001
Related: The Hope Entity, MC, Irreversibility Principle

Overview
The Desert is Subject-001’s inner psychological landscape, inherited from the original MC.
It first appears as an endless space where the MC crawls toward a glowing figure. Later, the image is understood as the sand inside an hourglass and as the internal path toward The Hope Entity.

Behavior
The Desert is not geographically stable. Distance, weather, light, and scale shift according to Subject-001’s coherence.
The Hope Entity does not move through the Desert. Instead, Subject-001’s ability to perceive and approach it changes.

Meaning
The Desert is where the project turns the theme of time into an image of trauma.
It does not offer escape from the broken world. It offers the possibility of integration within it.

Eleventh Chamber
Tags: project-zaman world location eleventh-chamber gibborim trauma established
”The room where grief became an instrument.”
Type: Cult chamber; preservation and psychological weapon
Era: Before the Oscillation
Controlled by: Gibborim, operated through Axios systems
Related: Alyna, MC, Shadow Form, Oscillation of Eras

Overview
The Eleventh Chamber holds Alyna’s preserved body.
Its reveal forces the original MC to confront Alyna’s death, the cult’s invasion of his grief, and the reduction of her body into an experimental object.

Function
The chamber is not merely storage. It is used as a final instrument of emotional destruction during the cult’s last phase of experimentation.
When the Eleventh Chamber is revealed, the original MC’s compassionate soul-form and Shadow Form enter maximum conflict.

Consequence
The Eleventh Chamber is the proximate trigger of the Oscillation of Eras.
It does not cause the catastrophe alone, but it tears open the wound created by Alyna’s death and exposes the contradiction the MC can no longer contain.

Faction Territory Split
Useful when placing encounters — The Oasis already divides the map by ideology:

The Mirage — cult facilities, abandoned laboratories, ritual sites, temporally distorted regions, areas under strong cult influence

That division does most of the work of a world map already. A player travelling toward the truth moves geographically away from safety.

Open Questions

Is the facility the main playable space? It is the emotional center of the entire backstory and is described as still standing in distorted form. Nothing yet says whether the player can enter it.
Are the mansion and the facility the same site? Story Structure has Alyna working as a garden worker “at the mansion” while the MC is held in “the facility,” and the garden is where her tombstone later appears. They read as one complex, but this is never stated.
Is the Desert enterable? Whether it is a playable area, a cutscene space, or a recurring interstitial changes a great deal about the game’s structure.
What is a “temporally distorted region” to walk through? Named in The Oasis as Mirage territory, never described.
Does Ashbourne still exist after the Oscillation? It survived the fire. Its post-Catastrophe state would be an obvious and powerful early location.
Where is the founder of The Oasis buried, or lost? A pilgrimage site both successor factions claim would give the schism a physical anchor.

project-zaman/world/setting/setting-over.content:
Setting Overview
Tags: project-zaman world index setting working


                  
                  Purpose of this folder 
                  
                

The physical and social world: what kind of place this is, what technology exists, who holds power, and what daily life looks like on both sides of the Catastrophe. Specific places go in World/Locations; the order of events goes in World/Era & Timeline.



Established
Period. An early 20th century world, fractured by the misuse of the soul (Project Zaman).
Two states of the world. The setting exists in two distinct conditions, and almost every note in the vault belongs to one or the other:



































Before the OscillationAfter the OscillationRealityIntactPermanently desynchronized; historical eras collide in the same spaceThe facilityOperationalA decayed, distorted structure suspended in temporal disarrayThe cultAnthropos public, Gibborim hidden, Axios recordingAll on-site scientists and personnel killedPopulationOrdinary society, newspapers, harbors, inns, mansionsLargely unaccounted for after the Fabrication DemiseOrganized humanityInstitutions, households, publishersFaction remnants: the Order of the Oasis and The Mirage
Social texture that already exists in the notes. Newspapers and media that can be steered by a respected family. Wealthy households that hire on reputation and discretion. A harbor with working women carrying loads. Rented flats with thin walls. Inns busy enough to disappear into. Secret publishers who can be tracked, shut down, and interrogated. Undercover troops passing as beggars, drunkards, and middle-class citizens. A charitable orphanage nobody thinks to question.
No ordinary civilians in play. The Oasis states the game contains no civilian population. Settlement regions function as protected territories, faction outposts, or remnants of organized human activity.
Power structure. Anthropos holds public legitimacy through charity, academic patronage, medical initiatives, and civic development. Gibborim directs it from behind separated chains of authority. Axios supplies the technical foundation for both. See Anthropos, Gibborim, Axios.

Open Questions

Where is this? No country, city, or region is named anywhere in the vault. Ashbourne, the harbor, and the mansion all exist without a map. Deciding whether to name the setting or keep it deliberately unplaced is a real choice with consequences for the naming framework.
How much technology? Weapons, wheelchairs, newspapers, and laboratory instruments appear. Whether there are cars, telephones, electric light, or trains has not been set, and it affects how Alyna’s underground network plausibly operates.
What does the collision of eras actually look like? “Different historical eras collide in the same space” is the single most distinctive feature of the post-Oscillation world and the least described. Which eras? Visible seams, or seamless? Can a player walk from one into another?
How long after the Oscillation does the playable story begin? Long enough for The Oasis to be founded, lose its founder, and split into two factions — but no duration is given.
Does anything outside the affected region survive? Whether the Oscillation is global or bounded determines whether “humanity” in The Oasis’s oath means everyone or only the survivors nearby.
Is the cult entirely gone? All on-site personnel died. Whether Gibborim survives elsewhere decides who the late-game antagonist actually is.


Suggested Notes for This Folder

The World Before the Oscillation — the intact society, for scenes set in the MC’s childhood and Alyna’s campaign
The World After the Oscillation — the playable present
Technology and Daily Life
Society and Class — Alyna’s uniform grants access precisely because of how this world sees servants
What Remains of Humanity — population, settlements, the Fabrication Demise




                  
                  Anchor to protect 
                  
                

The horror of this setting is institutional rather than supernatural. An orphanage, a respected family, a research division, a newspaper. The metaphysics only work because the ordinary world around them is completely believable.

Project ZAMAN — Design Overview
The Oscillation of Eras

A Soulslike set in an early 20th century world fractured by the misuse of the soul.

Engine: Unreal Engine 5/6 · New Input System
Genre: 3D Action / Adventure · Soulslike · Semi-OpenWorld
Aesthetic Inspirations: Lies of P, Bloodborne
Mechanics Inspirations: Lies of P, Black Myth Wukong, Sekiro

Synopsis
A Masonic cult misidentifies Immaculate Thought — the soul’s capacity to process meaning without contradiction at extreme speed — as time manipulation. Repeated exploitation shatters the soul, triggering Soul Fission and an irreversible desynchronization of reality: the Oscillation of Eras. The protagonist, an unnamed orphan bound in a double straitjacket, must navigate a broken world where restoration is impossible and adaptation is the only path forward.

Protagonist — The Original MC





























AttributeDetailIdentityUnnamed orphan. 188 cm, lean-muscled. Bound in a double straitjacket. Exists entirely outside the cult’s Hebrew naming system — a deliberate outsider.MiraclesPerceptual time quantification · Epistemological object contact · Silent connection across distance. All require internal calm to function.Dual FormsAn original empathetic self, who acts as a mediator, and a shadow form driven by vacancy and destruction — held in tension throughout the narrative.AlinaCaretaker turned eternal bond. Her death — accidental gunfire during a confrontation with Noam — is the Oscillation’s emotional catalyst. Her final instruction: stand for good, end evil, stay himself, resist the shadow.NoamAntagonist. Same age as the MC, physically similar. Groomed by his Masonic parents. His childhood report of the MC’s miracles unintentionally triggered the cult’s extraction. Decayed step by step into a full ideologue.

The Cult

























LayerNameSubtitlePublic FaceAnthropos (Greek)“In Service of All Mankind”Inner OrderGibborim (Hebrew — “those who overreached divinity”)“We Who Stood Beyond the Threshold”Science DivisionAxiom (public only, no private name)—
Symbols: White snake = Gibborim (hissing, anchor-hook tail) · Black snake = Axiom (silent, no hook)

World Lore

Ashbourne Children’s Home — Secretly owned by the cult as a capability pipeline.
The Desert — The MC’s psychological landscape.
The Hope Entity — The MC’s childhood self. Reconnection is not a return to innocence, but a reconciliation with the self.
The 11th Chamber — Contains Alina’s preserved corpse. Its unveiling caused both of the MC’s soul-forms to fluctuate at the same time, triggering the Oscillation.
Subject-002 (The Instrument) — Post-fission entity that keeps precision and clarity but lacks empathy and creativity. Hums a distorted lullaby. Shimmering skin with sigil markings. Eventual ally to the MC.


Core Principles
01 — Naming Framework
Arabic is used for core metaphysical truths, world concepts, and protagonist-facing ideas. Hebrew is used for the cult, its rituals, subjects, and esoteric terminology. The protagonist is named in neither, which reinforces his outsider status.
02 — The Irreversibility Principle
Nothing is restored. Only adaptation is possible. The Oscillation is permanent, and the world cannot be reset or saved in the conventional sense.
03 — Hope as Integration
The game’s central theme is adaptation, not restoration. Hope is understood as the integration of a fragmented self — not salvation, not escape.
04 — Dual Identity
The MC’s two forms are not good against evil in a simple binary. The shadow form is driven by vacancy, the original by empathy. The tension between them is the game’s internal drama.

Project ZAMAN is an original Soulslike in active development.
